correctness.rationale: Convex symmetrization reduces full symmetric-stochastic FMMC to two orbit variables. The exact product Laplacian eigenvalue branches give three constraints. Their positive-weight affine identity yields a global lower bound independent of those variables; explicit feasible edge weights attain it for all n. Endpoint comparisons bound every remaining Fourier mode. Exact rational characteristic-polynomial tests n=3,4,6 and independent matrix/LP tests n=3..60 passed. Numeric tests are corroboration, not infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The strongest inspected general formulas include the convex SDP reduction and an equal-edge-weight theorem for edge-transitive graphs. For all n except the cube n=4, prisms have separate rim and rung orbits, so those formulae do not determine their optimum. The full 2010 semi-cycle network with two vertices per group has alternating K_2,2 and matching seam blocks: for even K>=6 it has K/2 four-cycles, whereas C_K Cartesian K_2 has K four-cycles, proving these graph families are not isomorphic. The n=4 cube case is special and is not presented as individually new.

originality.rationale: The nearest checked primary work supplies convexity and graph symmetry, not the exact non-edge-transitive prism solution. The candidate solves the complete global symmetric mixing-rate optimization on every prism, with a unique orbit-invariant optimizer and asymptotically vanishing rung weight. The 2010 semi-cycle K-PPDR network is structurally distinct for cycle lengths at least six. A special cube case is already covered by edge-transitive methods. Unindexed equivalent formulas and stronger product theorems remain possible.

value.rationale: The canonical unbounded circular-ladder graph family has two structurally distinct transport directions. The exact optimal symmetric Markov design exhibits an unexpected diffusion-scale allocation: rim probability tends to 1/2 while rung probability shrinks as pi^2/n^2. The theorem completely determines the globally optimal spectral mixing value and all invariant optimal weights, with a tight three-mode lower-bound explanation. Its spectral gap is asymptotically twice that of the natural equal-edge lazy chain. This is a motivated network-design classification rather than an arbitrary small graph calculation.
